patients.summary: Logistics coordinator who joined in 2023 with hypertension on hydrochlorothiazide and recurrent calcium oxalate stones. Two ureteral stones in 2024 (right, CT-proven; left, clinical) passed after ED visits, then an adhesive small bowel obstruction in late 2025 from a 2013 open appendectomy, managed without surgery.

Has commercial PPO through work, card info taken. Takes one blood pressure pill. Booked new patient visit Tue 8/22 at 8:00 am, first slot since he starts work at 9:30. documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
45M new to the practice. Previous PCP was across town; records release signed, list requested.

Concerns today: none really. Wants his BP pill continued and a doctor he can text.

HTN: told he had high pressures at a work screening and then at his old office about four years ago. On HCTZ 25 mg every morning since, no side effects, no dizziness. Doesn't check at home.

Kidney stones: says he has had stones 'more than once' before coming here, all passed on their own, one of them was sent off and came back calcium oxalate. Can't give years without looking. His dad has had a string of stones too. Nothing recent.

PMH: hypertension, recurrent calcium oxalate stones.
PSH: open appendectomy around 2013, appendix had ruptured, a few days in the hospital. Nothing since.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.
Allergies: none to medications.
FH: father with recurrent kidney stones. Mother has hypertension.
SH: logistics coordinator for a distributor, a lot of time on the warehouse floor and on the phone. Never smoked. A drink or two a month at most. Lives alone in Amherst.

ROS: no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no headaches, no urinary symptoms, bowels regular.

Exam: vitals as recorded, BP fine. Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed RLQ transverse scar, no hernia. No CVA tenderness. Extremities without edema. Skin warm.

A/P
1. Essential hypertension, controlled on HCTZ 25. Continue. CMP for K, Na, Ca and creatinine.
2. Recurrent calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis, quiet. Encouraged steady water through the day. We can talk more about prevention if he gets another one.
3. Health maintenance: lipids, A1c, CBC. One-time hep C and HIV screen, he agrees. FIT kit given for colon cancer screening at 45. Tdap given today, last tetanus shot he thinks was in his twenties. PHQ-2 negative.

Follow up 6 months for BP, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Adam, your bloodwork from Tuesday is all in the normal range: kidney function, potassium and sodium (which we watch on hydrochlorothiazide), calcium, blood counts, cholesterol and sugar. Hep C and HIV screens were negative. Nothing to change. Don't forget to drop off that stool kit when you get a chance.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast
reports.text: Indication: right flank pain radiating to the groin, history of stones. Technique: axial non-contrast images of the abdomen and pelvis with coronal reformats. Findings: 5 mm calculus within the right ureter. No hydronephrosis. Both kidneys normal in size. Bladder unremarkable. Appendix surgically absent. No free fluid. Visualized bowel unremarkable.

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional emergency department, visit 06/04/2024. Brief note sent to primary care.

46 y/o M, known calcium oxalate stone former, on HCTZ for HTN. Two days of right flank pain, comes and goes in spasms, goes down into the groin. Nauseated, threw up twice. Denies fever, burning with urination or dark urine. NKDA. Prior appendectomy.

Exam: afebrile, BP 135/85. Right CVA tenderness. Abdomen otherwise soft.
UA: blood present, no pyuria, no bacteria.
CT A/P without contrast: 5 mm stone in the right ureter.

Treated with IV ketorolac and IV ondansetron with relief. Asked about what to eat to avoid more stones, told to take it up with his PCP.

Dx: right ureterolithiasis.
Dispo: home. Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily until passed, ibuprofen 600 mg q6h prn, ondansetron 4 mg ODT prn. Strain urine. Return for fever, uncontrolled pain or vomiting. PCP follow-up within 1 week.

documents.title: Kidney stone ER visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I ended up in the ER yesterday with another stone, right side this time, they said 5 mm. Got sent home with tamsulosin and pain pills. They told me to see you within a week. Also I'd like to finally talk about what I should be eating to stop getting these. Next Tuesday early morning works if you have it.

documents.title: RE: Kidney stone ER visit
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Sorry to hear it, Adam. You're booked Tue 6/11 at 7:40 am. Doctor says keep straining your urine and call or text if you get a fever or the pain gets out of hand.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: ED 6/4 for R flank pain, CT showed a 5 mm R ureteral stone. Passed it Friday 6/7 in the shower, felt a sharp twinge then relief; didn't catch it in the strainer. No pain since, off the ibuprofen and ondansetron, finishing tamsulosin today. No fever, no urinary symptoms.

Wants to talk prevention. Typical day: coffee in the morning, a water bottle he forgets in the truck, eats out at lunch a lot.

O: vitals as charted, afebrile. No CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft, nontender.
UA today: no blood.

A/P
1. R ureteral stone, passed. Resolved. Stop tamsulosin.
2. Recurrent calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis. Went through prevention: aim for enough fluid to make about 2.5 L of urine a day (he'll keep a 32 oz bottle at his desk and refill it three times), cut back on salty restaurant food, keep meat portions moderate, don't cut out dairy since normal calcium in food helps. HCTZ is also doing double duty here, so stays as is. Handout on low-oxalate foods given.
3. HTN: BP fine.

See in September for physical.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
46M annual exam.

Interval: R ureteral stone in June, passed after an ED visit. Says he's better about water on weekdays, worse on weekends. No flank pain since. BP meds no issues.

Meds: HCTZ 25 mg daily. NKDA.
Habits: never smoker, rare drink. Walks the warehouse all day, no other exercise. Sleep ok.
PHQ-2: 0.

ROS negative across systems.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. Eyes, ears, throat normal. No lymphadenopathy. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular without murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender, old appendectomy scar. No CVA tenderness. Normal gait. No edema. Skin without suspicious lesions.

A/P
- Health maintenance: CMP, lipids, CBC. FIT kit #2 given. Flu and COVID shots when the fall vaccines are in, nurse visit.
- HTN controlled, continue HCTZ.
- Nephrolithiasis: keep up the fluids.

Next physical in a year, BP check in between.

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional emergency department, date of service 12/14/2024 (Saturday). Copy faxed to PCP.

CC: L flank pain x3 hrs.
HPI: 46M with HTN and recurrent calcium oxalate stones, R ureteral stone in June. Today at work had abrupt onset of severe L flank pain, steady with surges that double him over, no better lying still or moving around. Nausea, emesis x2. No diarrhea, no dysuria, no fever. Admits he drinks very little water at work and a lot of tea, eats red meat most days.
Meds: HCTZ 25 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam: BP 152/92, HR 104, T 37.1. Restless, pacing the room, can't get comfortable. L CVA tenderness. Abdomen without rebound or guarding.
UA: microscopic hematuria, no pyuria or bacteriuria.

MDM: presentation typical for recurrent stone, prior CT-confirmed stone 6 months ago, no signs of infection. Imaging deferred. IV ketorolac, IV ondansetron, pain improved to tolerable.

Impression: L ureterolithiasis.
Plan: discharge. Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, ibuprofen 600 mg q6h prn, ondansetron 4 mg ODT q8h prn, strain urine. Return for fever or worsening pain. Increase fluids. PCP f/u.

documents.title: Another stone
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Back in the ER yesterday afternoon, left side this time. They didn't do a scan, said it was obviously another stone. Same meds as June. Pain is a dull ache today, the pills are handling it. Do I need to come in?

documents.title: RE: Another stone
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry you're dealing with this again. Keep straining and drink plenty. If you get a fever, chills, or pain the pills can't touch, go back in. Let's do a quick video visit Thursday so I can check how it's going. The front desk will reach out with a time.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from his car on lunch break, identity verified.

S: ED 12/14 for L flank pain, treated as a stone, no imaging there. Pain stopped abruptly Tuesday 12/17 evening, thinks it passed, strainer came up empty. No pain since, eating fine, no fever, urine looks normal. Stopped the ibuprofen Monday.

Candid that he slid on the water plan since summer. During the workday drinks maybe two cups of water, but 4 to 5 mugs of black tea, and red meat most nights.

O: comfortable on camera, speaking full sentences, no distress.

A/P
1. L ureteral stone, passed per symptoms. Resolved. Can stop tamsulosin.
2. Recurrent calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis, second stone this year. Went back over it: water first, tea is fine in moderation but black tea is high in oxalate so swap at least half for water, red meat a few nights a week rather than most, keep salt down. Continue HCTZ. He'll set phone reminders for water.
3. HTN: ED pressure was up with pain; recheck at next office visit.

Office visit in March for BP.
